title: Observability pipeline reshaper and pager-simulator for SLO-aware alerting
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket refactors parts of the observability ingestion and alerting pipeline to enable more deterministic SLO burn-rate calculations, better error/latency attribution, and introduces a 'pager simulator' tool to validate paging policies under realistic trace/metric perturbations.

Background and motivation:
- Current alerting suffers from noisy pages during scheduled bursts and transient tail-latency spikes. Root cause analysis is hampered because traces, logs, and metrics arrive with inconsistent enrichment (missing route/model tags, partial request ids) and our metric rollups smooth important short windows.
- We need an ingestion reshaper that: 1) enforces deterministic trace -> metric correlation keys, 2) performs lightweight adaptive downsampling on low-cardinality streams, and 3) emits a lane of telemetry optimized for burn-rate (short-window aggregations with preserved percentiles and error counts).
- The pager simulator will let SREs and oncall leads run policy experiments against historical and synthetic traffic, measuring page volume, precision/recall for high-burn periods, and time-to-detection under config changes.

Goals and success criteria (measurable):
- Reduce noisy pages attributed to transient bursts by 40% in the canary team over 4 weeks.
- Burn-rate calculation latency <= 15s for 1s and 5s windows, and <= 30s for 1m windows.
- Pager simulator can replay a day's traffic in < 10m and report page volume and false-positive rate.
- 95% of traces for sampled requests include route, model_version, customer_tier tags after ingestion.

Approach / Implementation plan:
1) Ingestion reshaper (metrics/logs pipeline changes):
   - Add a deterministic keying stage that synthesizes trace_metric_key = sha256(request_id || model_version || route) when available; fallback to sampled client_ip + route.
   - Emit short-window (1s/5s/1m) percentiles and error counts into a dedicated 'slo.burn' metrics namespace with labels preserved.
   - Implement adaptive downsampling on high-cardinality low-volume label combinations to reduce cardinality explosion while preserving heavy hitters.
   - Ensure structured logs include trace_metric_key and minimal context for fast attribution in dashboards.

2) Tracing hooks and enrichment:
   - Extend runtime trace hook to attach model_version and route early in request lifecycle. Instrumented SDKs will include a lightweight header (X-RW-TraceMeta) to avoid N+1 lookups.
   - Add a post-ingest enrichment job that backfills missing model_version using short-term KV cache correlated by request latency windows.

3) Pager simulator:
   - Simulator takes: historical metric stream exports (s3 path) + synthetic perturbation profiles (burst, ramp, gradual drift).
   - Evaluates current paging rules (burn-rate thresholds, no-pager windows, dedup heuristics) and outputs aggregated metrics: pages/day, median time-to-page, precision/recall vs known incidents.
   - Provide a UI/CLI to run scenarios and generate exportable reports for incident reviews.

4) Anomaly detection refinement:
   - Shift from purely statistical outlier detectors to a hybrid approach: short-window change-point detection for burn triggers, and a secondary Bayesian drift detector for gradual regressions.
   - Ensure anomaly signals feed the burn-rate pipeline as an auxiliary weight (helps avoid pages from one-off noisy signals).

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): deploy ingestion reshaper and tracing hooks for 1 product team (canary): week 1-2. Run pager simulator against last 7 days of telemetry and tune policy.
- Phase 2 (wider rollout): after 2 weeks of stable canary metrics and simulated policy runs, enable reshaper for 50% of traffic across internal tenants and re-evaluate page volume.
- Phase 3 (global): full rollout with operator opt-in flags and automated rollback if pages exceed threshold.

Migration and backward compatibility:
- All changes will be feature-flagged. A compatibility layer will accept both old and new trace keys and map them for 30 days. Dashboards include toggle to show legacy vs reshaped telemetry.

Observability and dashboards:
- New 'SLO Burn lab' dashboard (Grafana): short-window burn rates, page simulator output, precision/recall trends, percentile heatmaps by route/model.
- Error dashboard augmented with trace_metric_key links to jump-to-trace and to logs explorer.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/lab/obs-pipeline-reshaper
- Pager-sim prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pager-sim/pull/12
- Canaries dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/obs/canary-slo-burn

Risks and trade-offs:
- Deterministic keying may increase cardinality in some cases; mitigated by adaptive downsampling and per-tenant caps.
- Backfilling missing model_version could introduce lag; we will limit backfill window to 10m and mark synthetic fills in metadata.
- Simulator fidelity depends on quality of exported telemetry; we will provide guidance on minimal export schemas.

Next actions:
- [ ] Finalize schema for trace_metric_key and publish to SDK owners.
- [ ] Merge prototype PR for pager-sim and wire it into CI for nightly runs.
- [ ] Create canary runbook and escalation thresholds for the first deploy.
comments: 2026-02-06 - Liam Chen: Initial spike complete. Prototype of deterministic keying lives in an experimental branch (github.com/redwood-inference/obs-ingest/tree/reshaper-proto). Early results show 12% reduction in page duplication when keys exist.
2026-02-12 - SRE Review (Maya Flores): Concern about cardinality spikes for low-volume tenants. Suggest adding per-tenant cardinality caps and exposing droppped-count metrics to the dashboard.
2026-02-18 - Ava Patel: Incorporated SRE feedback. Added adaptive downsampling plan and a dropped_count metric to the 'slo.burn' namespace. Updated design doc link.
2026-02-25 - Data Eng (Ravi Kumar): Implemented a streaming enrichment stage in Flink. Backfill module will use a 10m micro-window and emit a deterministic flag. Deployed to staging.
2026-03-02 - PM Review (Sofia Martin): Approved canary scope. Requested pager simulator to support 'holiday traffic' synthetic profile for testing. Added to scope.
2026-03-07 - QA (Noah Price): Pager-sim replay test failed on large export files due to memory pressure. Added streaming replay mode and chunked ingestion to address.

2026-03-10 - Security (Elena Ortiz): Quick threat assessment - deterministic keys include request_id hashes only; avoid any PII. Confirmed headers will not carry user-identifiable info. Security review not required for release.

2026-03-12 - Liam Chen: Deployed reshaper for canary product team (10% traffic). Early telemetry: burn-rate calc latency ~13s for 1s windows. Pager simulator ran 24h replay in 7m. Next: tune downsampling thresholds.
